sources.title: Charity reflects on changing needs over 25 years

evidence.quote: Childline said Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram were the top platforms children named in counselling about online sexual abuse last year.
Simmons-Read said the social media ban for under 16s, which is due to come into force in 2027, "doesn't go far enough", could be bypassed
by criminals and could even discourage young people from speaking up about online grooming.
"We want tech platforms to invest more in detecting exploitation when it's happening on their platforms," he said.
Ellen Roome, from Cheltenham, who has been campaigning for improvements to online safety since the death of her son Jools in 2022, said not enough
is being done to protect young people on social media.
"Children are regularly being fed content that is either violent or grooming material and I think as it stands, there isn't any platform that is
fully safe for them," she said.
She works with schools to inform children how to be safe online, but said they are often unaware of the risks, including not viewing people
they meet online as strangers and expecting them to be "nasty" from the start.
The charity said in its early years it gave financial support to a number of larger community projects benefiting children but there was now an
increasing focus on helping individual children and families.
Applications for grants come in from social workers, health visitors, teachers, doctors, nurses and other frontline professionals and are considered individually by the charity's Directors.
The charity said the increasing focus on helping in individual cases meant providing something as "fundamental as a bed, flooring, white goods, clothing, safety equipment
or a heating appliance, as well as specialist disability equipment and educational opportunities".
These included the rising cost of living and increased demand for essential household items and practical support, it said.
The charity said it works through professional referrers who know the children and families involved.
